title: Value mapping play + demo script (sketch)
content:
Goal: quick one-page sales enablement deck + 5-min live demo script that maps Redwood inference value to platform/ML-engineering buyers. NOT a final slide deck — extremely tactical + copy-first.

Audience + use cases (target personas):
- Primary: Platform/ML infra engineers (concerned with latency, cost predictability, SLOs, rollout control)
- Secondary: Product engineering leads (care about feature velocity, quality regressions, reliability)
- Use cases to lead with: chat assistants at scale, embeddings search for customer support, reranking pipelines (ecom), sentiment/triage at low latency

Top 3 value props (one-liners to start slide headers):
1) Predictable latency at scale — dedicated pools + smart routing to hit 95th p99 targets without surprise cost spikes
2) Unit-economics control — batching/caching suggestions + quantization recipes that cut token cost 2–5x in real workloads
3) Safe rollouts and observability — per-route traces, eval-driven regression alerts, automatic fallbacks for reliability

Pricing framing (short):
- Start with cost-per-token baseline for comparable model families. Then show incremental delta for Dedicated vs Hosted (highlight locked-in unit cost vs burst flexibility).
- Quick rule of thumb to give in discovery: "For a mid-size product (2M tokens/mo steady), Dedicated saves ~30–40% vs hosted at 95% utilization" (estimate — call ops for exact)
- Offer: "Dedicated trials with 2-week capacity ramp + SLA evaluation" (placeholder for sales ops approval)

Competitive quick-differentiators (use as one-side-liners on a slide):
- vs public LLM APIs: we give deterministic throughput controls and on-prem options for regulated data (so SLOs & compliance without bespoke infra)
- vs self-hosted runtimes: we provide unified rollout tooling, auto-scaling policies, and observability out-of-the-box (so less ops work to get to production)
- vs other inference platforms: stronger unit-econ controls (intelligent batching + KV caching) and explicit rollback/fallback policies

Objection handling matrix (short answers you can use verbatim):
Q: "Why not just self-host?"
A: "Self-hosting can look cheap until you add on engineering time for KV cache logic, autoscaling, kernel tuning, and SRE overhead. Redwood gives those patterns as managed products with versioning + rollouts so you ship faster and predictable cost."

Q: "We need on-prem — can you run in our network?"
A: "Yes — Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packaging with KMS integrations. We can scope a proof-of-concept to run behind your network policies."

Q: "How do you avoid model regressions when we update weights or quantize?"
A: "Built-in eval hooks and canary rollouts tied to your prompt sets; we alert on quality regressions and automatically fallback to the previous stable model."

5-min demo script (concise, for SDR/AE quick call):
1) 0:00–0:30 — One sentence value prop + example customer ("Ecommerce search reranker: 3x better CTR at 40% lower latency after switching to Redwood dedicated pipeline")
2) 0:30–1:30 — Show Console: route config (region + fallback policy) and per-route SLO dashboard (latency percentiles + cost per token)
3) 1:30–2:30 — Show Rollouts: canary config, linked evals (prompt set + metrics), and auto-fallback policy
4) 2:30–3:30 — Show Optimize tips: batching suggestions and quantization recommendation for selected model + estimated cost delta
5) 3:30–4:30 — Quick trace of a request showing prefix caching hit and token-level cost breakdown
6) 4:30–5:00 — Next steps: propose a 2-week dedicated trial, provide sample prompt set to run evals

One-page battlecard (talking points for field):
- Elevator: "Redwood Inference gives you predictable, cost-effective LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with first-class observability and rollout controls."
- When to use: migrating from ad-hoc self-hosting; needing SLAs for inference; wanting to reduce per-token spend without sacrificing latency
- Price leash: be explicit about utilization assumptions when quoting savings
- Must-ask discovery q's: average concurrent requests, 95th/99th latency targets, data residency needs, existing model families & quantization tolerance

Demo artifacts checklist (what to prepare before demo):
- Customer prompt set (3–5 representative prompts) — ask prior to call
- Target SLOs (p50/p95/p99) and current cost per request
- Example model family and sequence length distribution
- Billing contact for potential Dedicated trial

Leave-behind assets (links we should attach to follow-up email):
- One-pager: short value mapping vs self-hosting and vs public APIs (draft in progress)
- Guide: "What to expect in a 2-week Dedicated trial" (SRE checklist, metrics we collect)
- Pricing note: example cost model for 1M/5M/10M tokens

Open questions / TODOs (work-in-progress items to resolve before finalizing deck):
- Need final approved savings percentages from finance for the "30–40%" line — ticketed GTM-778
- Update screenshot for Console UI after recent UX change (PR #89) — Marco to get new export
- Pull latency bench for 8k-token context models for hosted vs dedicated (ask infra bench team)
- Decide on standard prompt sets for demo (search + chat + embeddings)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep slide count to 6: cover problem, value props, quick demo, pricing framing, battlecard bullets, next steps
- Don't oversell quantization (call out potential accuracy tradeoffs)
- Add tiny case study box: "Retail customer — 18% reduction in latency p95, 2x throughput" (need approval from customer success)

Quick copy snippets for outreach (short lines AEs can paste):
- "Can I show you how we reduced p95 latency and monthly token cost for teams running search at 99th percentile SLOs? 10-min demo and a 2-week trial available."
- "We provide production rollouts with automatic fallbacks — important for teams that can't tolerate silent model regressions."

Version history/notes:
- v0.1 (2026-01-15) initial sketch
- v0.2 (2026-02-20) added demo script + competitors
- v0.3 (2026-03-10) updated tagging and shared with Liam/Sofia for review

End of sketch — feedback requested: tighten pricing framing and confirm bench numbers.
